title: Permission Scoping Wizard and Member Simulation Preview
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Admins need a fast, low-risk way to create and assign roles in RBAC v2 that precisely limit access (by resource, environment, model, and action) and to understand the effective permissions a member will have after group mappings and transitive grants. Current console flows are scattered: role creation is a form, scoping is implicit, and there is no pre-assignment simulation. Goal: Design a Permission Scoping Wizard paired with a Member Simulation Preview pane that lets admins build a role with explicit scope and then preview (or simulate) the effective permissions for a specific user or group before committing changes. The feature should: (1) surface granular scoping controls (resource selectors, environment tags, model-version selectors), (2) provide a readable policy expression builder for advanced policies, (3) show transitive grants and SSO group mappings, (4) include a "Preview as" simulation sandbox that connects to audit log and shows sample API operations that would be allowed/denied, and (5) include clear microcopy and a "danger zone" summary to prevent privilege creep. Constraints: must integrate with SSO/SAML group mappings, work with large orgs (thousands of groups), and avoid heavy client-side evaluation for performance/security reasons. UX should be accessible and mobile-responsive.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard flow allows creating a role with: name, description, permission set, explicit resource scope, environment tags, and optional policy expression.
Simulation Preview can run for a chosen user or group and returns a list of example allowed/denied API operations and a concise summary of transitive grants (group memberships, role inheritance).
Console shows an inline warning if the role includes write/delete actions at org-level and requires an explicit acknowledgement before save.
SSO group mapping panel shows mapped IdP groups that will be affected and highlights differences between direct and transitive assignments.
Simulation results link to the audit log (time-window + sample query) and include a note about eventual consistency for recently-changed mappings.
Design handoff includes annotated Figma screens, copy variants for all microcopy, and a small interaction spec for the simulation API contract used by engineering.
comments: 2026-03-11 Asha: Initial draft of the wizard flow. Focused on scoping by resource type (Model, Deployment, Dataset), environment tags (prod/staging), and an optional advanced policy expression editor for power users.

2026-03-12 Oliver: Reviewed wireframes. Asked for a compact default view for small screens and requested that the "Preview as" simulation be available as a non-blocking side panel. Flagged performance concerns for simulating users with large group memberships.

2026-03-12 Lina (PM): Suggested adding a sample API operation list in the preview to make results actionable for developers. Proposed a copy variant for the danger acknowledgment: 'I understand this role grants org-level write access'.

2026-03-13 Mark (Eng): Engineering notes — simulation will call a server-side evaluation service; we need to add a cache layer keyed by (role-hash, user-hash) to avoid re-computation for identical queries. We also should rate-limit simulation endpoints and return partial results if evaluation hits size limits.

2026-03-13 Priya (SecEng): Security review requested. Concerned about leaking group membership in preview; recommend masking full group lists by default and showing counts with an expandable disclosure. Also suggested logging each simulation request in audit logs with a special event type.

2026-03-14 Hana (Design): Iteration 2 uploaded to Figma with updated microcopy, error states, and an accessibility checklist. Uploaded link to prototypes and annotated interactions. Ready for handoff once security feedback is addressed.
2026-03-14 Oliver: Created ENG tasks for simulation API and caching (ENG-75123, ENG-75124). Assigned to backend infra. Added acceptance criteria related to audit log linkage.
decision_log: Use server-side policy evaluation for Simulation Preview to avoid inconsistent client logic and to allow central logging.
Mask detailed SSO group names by default in the preview (show '> N groups' with expand to reveal names for users with explicit permission and owner role).
Implement a rate-limited, cache-backed simulation API with TTL of 10 minutes for identical (role, user) queries.
Danger acknowledgment modal required for roles that include any '*:write' or 'org:*' permissions.
next_steps: Resolve security feedback: define exact audit event schema for simulation requests (Priya/P#).
Engineering to produce an API contract doc for simulation endpoint (ENG-75123).
Design to finalize mobile responsive layouts and microcopy variants (Hana).
PM to prepare customer-facing release notes and admin guide examples showing common scoping patterns (Lina).
Schedule design-eng sync on 2026-03-18 to unblock implementation.
risk: Potential info exposure in simulation if group membership lists are shown without access checks.
High-cardinality group mappings could make simulation slow; need to cap evaluation or return progressive results.
Admins might over-index on simulation 'allowed operations' samples and miss real-world edge cases; include clear caveats about sample nature.
notes: UX principle: make the safest choice the easiest — default scoping should be conservative and expanding scope should be explicit.
Consider adding a one-click 'compare with existing roles' feature in a future iteration to help admins avoid duplication.
